status: authored compatibility policy, not browser support

same: Use one instance of the same recipe; merge named layers rather than duplicate paint.
flat-depth: Strict flat modeling excludes relief, cast, lensing, gloss or emission. Use another receiver or relax the flat intent explicitly.
body-model: These complete body models demand incompatible opaque/transmitting or flat/volume assumptions on one receiver. Choose one body; the other can style a separate child.
acquire: One acquisition/blur/tint graph only. Coalesce overlapping glass layers; do not stack two backdrop filters or claim native equivalence.
native: Native Mica/Liquid Glass behavior is only partially sourced and not a portable CSS preset. Keep a verified opaque/web fallback; independent receiver only where acquisition differs.
body-field: Both affect the body color field. Declare one base and one masked overlay with explicit order/interpolation; do not blindly multiply complete fills.
volume: Pick one signed relief profile and one key light; a concavity and convexity can coexist only on separate local regions.
emission: Resolve to one named inner/outer emission graph with a readable semantic core. Do not sum repeated halos or use bloom as focus.
content: Letterpress is restricted to a separate reviewed display inscription. Functional glyph/text remains plain; never stack reflected and emitted type by default.
texture: Use one static texture owner/seed and keep reading regions clear. Existing Acrylic noise is edited, not doubled.
edge: Use one perimeter owner and contour, preserve required edges, and fit decorative gradient/bevel inside the available rim.
cast: Only the receiver's existing Surface cast is allowed; merge source lobes once. Flat and inflow controls still have no cast.
referent: The physical/historical language needs a coherent referent and role scope. A primitive alone does not reproduce the entire visual language.
separate: Channels are distinct and can coexist on an eligible receiver under shared light, contrast and role caps; this is not a certification of arbitrary parameter values.
